name: How long does a design-build home addition take in Pasadena or Glendale?

mainEntity.name: How long does a typical design-build addition take from first meeting to completion in Pasadena or Glendale?
mainEntity.text: How long does a typical design-build addition take from first meeting to completion in Pasadena or Glendale?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic timeline depends on project size and complexity. Smaller additions may take a few months for design and permitting, followed by several more months of construction. Larger additions or custom remodels can take much longer if the home has structural complications, hillside conditions, or extensive permit review. In Pasadena and Glendale, time can also be affected by neighborhood-specific requirements, historic review, and the completeness of the initial plans. The design-build process often saves time by overlapping design, pricing, and constructability review, but homeowners should still expect early planning to take longer than they think. A good firm should give a phased schedule that separates preconstruction, permit processing, demolition, structural work, and finish work. The best way to avoid delays is to make decisions early, approve selections quickly, and confirm long-lead items before construction starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A design-build home addition often takes several months to more than a year, depending on scope, permits, and site conditions. Smaller additions may move faster, while larger custom additions can take longer because of design revisions, city approvals, structural work, and material lead times. The planning phase can be as important as the build phase.
